strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clear articulation of data quality bottleneck with specific failure modes (low pedagogical value, overfitting trap)
Rigorous methodology: Formal verification ensures soundness (Propositions 4.1, 4.3); clear formalization of invariant quality properties
Solid experimental validation: Multiple model scales (0.6B-8B), strong baselines, three runs with error bars, comprehensive ablation study
Practical significance: 4B model matching 120B GPT-OSS is valuable for deployment; VBP metric better reflects real scenarios
Reproducibility: Detailed hyperparameters, configuration details, and commitment to release code/models/datasets
Clear presentation: Well-written with effective examples (Figures 2, 3, 5) and intuitive pipeline design
weaknesses: Severely limited scope: Only one verifier (UAutomizer) and one benchmark set (SV-COMP); no evidence of generalization despite identifying this as a limitation; evaluation on only 123 hard instances
Brittle LLM dependency: Simplification requires proprietary Kimi K2 model; not semantics-preserving; no analysis of failure modes when simplification produces weak candidates
Missing sensitivity analyses: Choice of N=4 candidates, verbosity threshold η, and grade threshold Q≥2 all lack justification or ablation studies
Incomplete comparison with large models: Unclear how GPT-5.2/GPT-OSS-120B were prompted; inference latency excluded from main metrics despite practical importance (only in VBPE2E)
No statistical significance testing: Three runs is limited; some confidence intervals overlap (e.g., Table 3: Qwen3-8B vs GPT-5.2), but no formal tests conducted
Limited technical novelty: AST normalization is straightforward; LLM simplification is intuitive but not novel; main contribution is pipeline engineering rather than fundamental insight

Insufficient failure analysis: No systematic study of when/why WONDA fails; small improvements on some metrics (Qwen3-0.6B: 12.2%→14.1%) raise practical significance questions; timeout resolution remains unexplained
Evaluation limited to hard instances only: No results on full benchmark set (easy + hard), limiting generalizability claims; potential selection bias toward problems where data curation helps

strengths: Well-motivated problem: raw verifier outputs are poor training signals due to syntactic noise and overfitting to tool artifacts
Rigorous formalization: formally defines desired invariant properties and provides soundness proofs for the normalization pipeline
Systematic two-stage design: clear decomposition into AST normalization (with formal rewrite rules) and LLM-guided semantic simplification
Strong ablation study (Table 4): clearly demonstrates the value of each pipeline stage, showing V2 provides substantial gains over V0 and V1
Multi-scale evaluation: tests across three model sizes (0.6B, 4B, 8B) rather than single model, showing consistent improvements
Reproducibility: commits to releasing code, models, and curated datasets
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core contributions are incremental—AST normalization is straightforward, LLM-based rewriting is standard in data curation, and VBP metric is a minor contribution

Overstated claims: (1) Title 'Not All Invariants Are Equal' doesn't reflect the actual contribution about data cleaning; (2) Claims 4B-V2 'matches' GPT-OSS-120B, but Table 3 shows VBP 165.5±3.2 vs 165.8±5.6 (within error bars, statistically indistinguishable)

Single verifier only: evaluated only with UAutomizer for both training data source and baseline. No validation on other verifiers (Eldarica, etc.), limiting generalizability and raising subtle verifier-specific bias concerns
Small evaluation set: only 123 hard instances, of which 20 (16.3%) timeout for baseline, reducing statistical power and coverage. No significance testing performed despite overlapping error bars

Methodological issues: (1) Quality Grade definition (Def 4.2) compares aggregate baseline time (median over 3 runs) with single-run verification time—not directly comparable; (2) Mixing grade-2 (no speedup) and grade-3 (with speedup) samples during training is unexplained; (3) LLM simplification success rate not reported

Unvalidated core claims: the 'overfitting trap' and 'pedagogical value' motivations are stated but never empirically validated. Data leakage: training invariants sourced from UAutomizer while UAutomizer serves as baseline creates subtle verifier-specific optimization
Modest improvements: 12-20 second reduction on ~193s baseline = 6-10% improvement in absolute terms; practically meaningful gains are limited

Missing analysis: (1) No introspection into why V2 invariants are 'more learnable'; (2) No ablation on LLM parameters (N=4 candidates, temperature, etc.); (3) Unclear how many V2 samples come from actual LLM rewriting vs. just normalized invariants; (4) Algorithm 2 fallback bias unquantified

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear identification of data quality issues (pedagogical value and overfitting trap) grounded in concrete examples
Rigorous methodological framework with formal definitions of good training invariants and soundness proofs (Propositions 4.1, 4.3)
Comprehensive pipeline design combining AST normalization, LLM-driven semantic rewriting, and formal verification with clear transformation goals
Strong experimental results across multiple model scales (0.6B-8B) showing consistent improvements—4B model matches 120B parameter baselines
Thorough ablation study (Table 4) demonstrating the contribution of each pipeline stage (normalization adds ~8-10% correctness; simplification doubles speedup rate)
Practical significance: demonstrates smaller language models can match much larger models with better data, important for deployment
Excellent presentation with clear figures, comprehensive appendix, and strong reproducibility commitment (code/models/datasets promised)
Novel VBP metric appropriately captures portfolio-based deployment where LLM and verifier run in parallel
weaknesses: Limited evaluation scope: single verifier backend (UAutomizer) for both data curation and evaluation; only 123 hard instances from InvBench; no evaluation on other verifiers (Eldarica, DIARICAc) or benchmarks raises serious generalization concerns

Circular dependency on UAutomizer: training data derived from UAutomizer outputs, models evaluated on UAutomizer-solvable problems; while framed as addressing overfitting trap, still fundamentally relies on same teacher, leaving unclear whether model learns verification principles or tool artifacts

Missing comparisons: no comparison with alternative data curation strategies, verifier-guided training, or reinforcement learning approaches; makes it difficult to assess whether WONDA is optimal vs. merely good
Unresolved challenge with hard cases: 'Solved' metric shows only 2-4 baseline timeouts resolved per run (Table 3); VBP metric excludes timeouts which may mask practical limitations

Inference latency treatment: main metrics exclude model latency to isolate capability; VBPₑ₂ₑ relegated to small mentions despite practical importance; for real deployment, latency differences between SLMs and large models are material

Gap between correctness and speedup improvements: while correctness rates roughly double, speedup rates improve more modestly (11%→25%); S̄>1 values (8-12x) reasonable but modest; ~6-10% VBP improvement suggests many generated invariants don't accelerate verification

Limited error analysis: no systematic characterization of failure modes, when/why fine-tuned models fail, or what invariant classes are difficult; Figure 3 shows single success with limited failure discussion

LLM simplification design choices underexplored: uses Kimi K2 for curation but Qwen3 for evaluation (unclear why); only N=4 candidates (no ablation); verbose threshold η not ablated; computational cost of curation pipeline not reported

Data quality distribution not fully analyzed: training set has ~62% Grade 2 (correct, no speedup) and 38% Grade 3; no ablation on whether including non-accelerating invariants helps learning or should be excluded
Potential data leakage: training and evaluation both from InvBench ecosystem; expansion from 219→362 instances via loop decomposition could inflate statistics; should be explicitly addressed

strengths: Clear problem motivation: Table 4 convincingly demonstrates that fine-tuning on raw verifier output (V0) degrades performance (e.g., Qwen3-4B Rvalid drops from 99.2% to 81.3%), providing strong empirical justification for the work

Strong and consistent empirical results: Qwen3-4B-V2 matches GPT-OSS-120B on VBPE2E (165.7s vs 167.6s, ~20× size difference), and Qwen3-14B-V2 matches GPT-5.2 (162.9s vs 163.4s); improvements consistent across model families (2-3× gains)

Rigorous experimental evaluation: Multiple model families and scales (0.6B–14B), three runs with error bars, proper train/val split, comprehensive ablations (V0→V1→V2), both hard and easy splits with well-defined metrics

Sound methodology: Formal verification acts as safety net (Propositions 4.1, 4.3 correct); quality grading (Definition 4.2) provides principled filtering; verification procedure is sound per Section 3.2

Excellent reproducibility: Complete hyperparameters (Tables 6-8), prompts (Appendix B), algorithms (Appendix C), UAutomizer config (Table 9), dataset statistics (Appendix D), and hardware specs provided
Practical utility: Pipeline is implementable and addresses real bottleneck in program verification; could make small models deployable in practice
Well-written presentation: Clear motivation, effective examples (Figures 1, 3, 5, 6), well-structured methodology, comprehensive appendices
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: Core techniques are known individually (AST normalization is standard compiler optimization; LLM-driven augmentation and formal verification filtering are established). Contribution is showing this specific combination works—more engineering than fundamental insight

Generalization concerns: (1) Single verifier source (UAutomizer only) limits coverage; models may inherit solver biases; (2) Only evaluated on InvBench (123 hard, 239 easy instances), a modest benchmark by modern standards; (3) All training data from UAutomizer-solvable programs—unclear generalization to programs UAutomizer cannot solve

Incomplete component ablation: Table 4 shows V0→V1→V2 progression, but doesn't separately quantify contributions of: normalization alone, LLM simplification alone, or data augmentation (N=4 candidates generating 6,584 from 2,995 verbose invariants). Unclear which component drives improvements

Missing sensitivity analyses: No ablations on verbosity threshold η (fixed at 20), number of candidates N (fixed at 4), or individual transformation goals (range generalization, constraint factoring, etc.). Prompt engineering choices under-justified

Normalization soundness caveat: Authors acknowledge that stripping integral type casts 'can break soundness under certain overflow conditions' but prioritize 'logical clarity.' While verified downstream, the normalization step itself isn't guarantee-sound
Hard problem limitations: Only resolves ~3/20 baseline timeouts (Table 3, Solved column); approach doesn't solve the hardest instances despite strong gains on easier problems

Training set scale and analysis: 7,284 samples is small by modern LLM standards; no analysis of scaling properties or data efficiency; no human evaluation of whether simplified invariants are genuinely more learnable

Model dependency risk: LLM simplification relies on Kimi K2 Thinking (proprietary model), raising reproducibility concerns if model is deprecated; generalization to other simplification engines unexplored

strengths: Clear problem formulation: Articulates well that data quality, not just model scale, is a bottleneck for neural invariant synthesis, distinguishing low pedagogical value from solver bias
Rigorous formal framework: Grounded in Hoare logic with formal guarantees (Propositions 4.1, 4.3); quality grading scheme (Definition 4.2) operationalizes 'high-quality' training data

Comprehensive experimental methodology: Extensive appendices with prompts, hyperparameters, algorithms; ablation study (V0→V1→V2) clearly demonstrates component contributions; multiple model families tested
Consistent improvements across model families: Demonstrates gains on Qwen3, Llama-3.1, and Mistral families, suggesting the approach generalizes across architectures
Honest limitations discussion: Acknowledges UAutomizer dependence and unresolved timeout cases without over-claiming; appropriate ethical statement
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core components are standard (AST normalization, LLM-based rewriting, straightforward grading); contribution is primarily engineering-focused combination of existing techniques, lacking conceptual innovation for a top-tier venue

Overstated frontier model comparisons: Claims like 'Qwen3-4B matches GPT-OSS-120B' ignore that correctness differs significantly (44.4% vs 58.0%); timing matches partly due to faster inference for small models. Primary metric (VBP) shows 7.5s gap to GPT-5.2 for Qwen3-14B while correctness trails by ~29 percentage points
Modest absolute performance: Hard-split correctness remains low (44-45%) limiting practical deployment in safety-critical verification; only ~3 timeouts resolved per model among 20 unsolved instances

Narrow evaluation scope: Single benchmark (123 hard instances is small), single verifier (UAutomizer), single task (loop invariants); no cross-verifier robustness evaluation or comparison with iterative approaches (Lemur, Loopy)

Unresolved distributional bias: Entire pipeline calibrated on UAutomizer outputs; acknowledged risk of learning solver-specific artifacts rather than general invariant properties, but no empirical validation of cross-verifier generalization
Unexplained performance degradation: V0 causes significant validity drops (Qwen3-4B: 99.2%→81.3%, Mistral-7B: 93.8%→65.0%) without thorough analysis of causation

Methodological concerns: Grading relies on noisy wall-clock timing comparisons (3 runs, single median); threshold η=20 for 'verbose' appears arbitrary; VBS metric assumes unrealistic parallel execution without resource contention
Missing sensitivity analyses: No evaluation of robustness to η threshold, LLM candidate count, simplification prompt design, or computational cost of curation pipeline (LLM API calls, expense)
Limited domain coverage: Findings apply only to C loop invariants; generalization to other languages, verification tasks, or solvers unexplored
Artificial end-to-end metrics: VBPE2E conflates logic time and inference latency, favoring small models; GPT-5.2 inference latency not disclosed, making fair comparison impossible

strengths: Clear problem motivation with compelling insight that data quality, not model scale, is the key bottleneck for neural invariant synthesizers
Technically sound methodology with formal guarantees: AST normalization soundness proven (Prop 4.1) and pipeline soundness guaranteed (Prop 4.3) via verification
Impressive empirical results: 4B model outperforms 80B off-the-shelf model (20× size reduction) and matches GPT-5.2 on end-to-end verification time without test-time compute overhead

Rigorous experimental evaluation with comprehensive ablations (Table 4) clearly isolating each component's contribution, consistent improvements across three model families, and proper statistical reporting (mean ± std over 3 runs)
Well-designed quality grading scheme (Def 4.2) that rewards both correctness AND speedup, reflecting practical verification needs
Excellent reproducibility: released code, comprehensive hyperparameters, full prompts, detailed dataset statistics, and hardware specifications enabling reliable reproduction
Clear presentation with effective use of running examples, informative visualizations (especially Pareto frontier in Figure 4), and thorough appendices
weaknesses: Limited novelty: individual components (AST normalization, LLM-based augmentation, formal verification) are standard techniques; the approach is primarily their integration applied to Wei et al. (2025)'s framework rather than fundamental innovation

Narrow scope with uncertain generalization: limited to C programs with UAutomizer backend; unclear extension to other languages/verifiers; risks inheriting UAutomizer's biases; evaluation on single benchmark suite

LLM simplification process lacks transparency and semantic guarantees: relies on proprietary Kimi K2 model for curation (reproducibility risk), semantics not preserved by design (only by post-hoc verification), no analysis of candidate rejection rates or sensitivity to N and η hyperparameters

Circular dependency in methodology: WONDA uses one LLM (Kimi K2) to curate training data that is then used to fine-tune different models, making it unclear whether improvements come from curation strategy or specific LLM used

Incremental improvement magnitudes: 2× improvement in correctness/speedup rate while consistent is modest; end-to-end VBPE2E gains partially attributable to VBS strategy combining with baseline, making it harder to isolate WONDA's specific contribution

Limited experimental scope: only 123 hard test instances (small test set); 20 instances still timeout even for best models limiting conclusions on hardest problems; no comparison with alternative data curation strategies; frontier model comparisons indirect (different problem formulations)

Missing sensitivity analyses: no ablation isolating LLM simplification step specifically; no investigation of hyperparameter sensitivity (η=20 char threshold, N=4 candidates, g≥2 grade threshold); limited discussion of failure cases

Dataset dependency: training set (7,284 samples) restricted to programs UAutomizer can verify, potentially biasing toward UAutomizer-friendly instances; timing-based quality grading (tv < tb) in Definition 4.2 could be noisy without sensitivity analysis provided
